meridian_skill.description: Universal migration from Obsidian, Notion, Logseq, markdown, CSV, JSON, Roam
meridian_skill.name: migrate

sections.heading: Contract
lines: Every migrated page is verified round-trip: written to gbrain, read back, spot-checked
Cross-references from the source system (wikilinks, block refs, tags) are converted to gbrain equivalents
Migration is tested on a sample (5-10 files) before bulk execution
Post-migration health check confirms page count, link integrity, and embedding coverage

sections.heading: Contract — steps
lines: Source data is never modified or deleted; migration is additive only

sections.heading: Obsidian Migration
lines: Import the vault directory into gbrain (Obsidian vaults are markdown directories)
`extract links` natively parses `[[relative/path]]` and `[[relative/path|Display Text]]`
alongside standard `[text](page.md)` markdown syntax. Ancestor-search resolution handles
wiki KBs where authors omit one or more leading `../` prefixes. The `.md` suffix is
inferred automatically for wikilinks
Obsidian-specific:
Tags (`#tag`) become gbrain tags
Frontmatter properties map to gbrain frontmatter
Attachments (images, PDFs) are noted but handled separately via file storage

sections.heading: Notion Migration
lines: Export from Notion: Settings > Export > Markdown & CSV
Notion exports nested directories with UUIDs in filenames
Strip UUIDs from filenames for clean slugs
Map Notion's database properties to frontmatter
Import the cleaned directory into gbrain

sections.heading: CSV Migration
lines: Use a designated column as the slug (e.g., name)
Use another column as compiled_truth (e.g., notes)
Store each page in gbrain

sections.heading: CSV Migration — steps
lines: For each row in the CSV, create a page with column values as frontmatter

sections.heading: Verification
lines: After any migration:
Check gbrain statistics to verify page count matches source
Export pages from gbrain for round-trip verification
Spot-check 5-10 pages by reading them from gbrain
Test search: search gbrain for "someone you know is in the data"

sections.heading: Verification — steps
lines: Check gbrain health for orphans and missing embeddings

sections.heading: Anti-Patterns
lines: **Skipping verification.** A migration without post-import health check, page count comparison, and spot-check reads is incomplete

sections.heading: Anti-Patterns — steps
lines: Never import the full dataset before verifying with 5-10 files. The cost of cleaning up hundreds of bad pages is enormous
Migration is additive. Never modify, move, or delete the source files
Wikilinks, block refs, and tags from the source system must be converted to gbrain equivalents. Dropping them loses the knowledge graph
